messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: SEV2 - Elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts observed for customer NimblePay on dedicated cluster dc-us-west-2-7. Alert fingerprints: 5xx-rate>5% over 5m, gateway-524 spikes. Paging SRE oncall.
Alice (oncall): I got the page, looking at dashboards now. Can someone paste the raw alert links?
Ben R. (eng-runtime): logs: https://grafana/reports/alerts/3895001234 - main signal is 5xx from inference-gateway returning 524/502. Backend runtime showing queued_inflight spike and kv-cache eviction rate up 20x.
Alice (oncall): kv evictions? that's usually noisy tenant. Carmen, can you check cluster allocation and pod restarts?
Carmen P. (platform): checking k8s. Node pool nodegroup-dc7 has 3 nodes with high GPU mem and high CPU steal. A few pods in pool-dc7-runtime are OOM/killed in past 12m: pod/runtime-xyz restartCount=6.
Raj (CS): NimblePay says their customers are seeing errors in prod, some long-running batches. They've opened a ticket and want ETA. I told them we're investigating.
Alice (oncall): Ok primary impacts: (1) 5xx from gateway to customer model routes, (2) elevated request latency, (3) some 524 upstream timeouts. Short-term: throttle the noisy tenant if we can, apply circuit breaker on their heavy routes, and add routing fallback for critical NimblePay endpoints to a degraded model variant.
Ben R. (eng-runtime): I can push a tenant throttle via internal CLI. Command:
```
redwoodctl tenant throttle --tenant nimblepay --qps 10 --duration 30m
```
that will shed excessive concurrency from tenant while preserving low-rate requests.
Taylor (rotating-oncall): I can run that now if Alice approves.
Alice (oncall): Do it. Also start a temporary canary route: map nimblepay-critical -> model-x-small (lower mem, faster kernel) for 5% of traffic. Ben, can you add that route?
Ben R. (eng-runtime): Creating route:
```
redwoodctl routes create --tenant nimblepay --route critical-fallback --model model-x-small --pct 5
```
Applying... done. Traffic shift started.
ops-bot: action-log: tenant throttle applied (nimblepay) by Taylor at 3895001305, route critical-fallback created by Ben R. at 3895001320.
Carmen P. (platform): I'm adding capacity: spinning up 2 more nodes in nodegroup-dc7 (G5xlarge equivalent). kubernetes autoscaler is at max for that pool. Running:
```
kubectl scale nodegroup nodegroup-dc7 --replicas=5
```
Request submitted to infra, ETA ~4-6 minutes to new nodes ready.
Alice (oncall): While nodes come up, check KV cache hit rates per tenant. If nimblepay is causing prefix churn, we should increase cache limits for other tenants temporarily.
Ben R. (eng-runtime): Prom query for evictions:
```
sum(rate(runtime_kv_evictions_total[1m])) by (tenant)
```
Output: nimblepay=128/s, tenant-foo=2/s, tenant-bar=1/s. Confirmed nimblepay dominating evictions.
Alice (oncall): That's the noisy neighbor right there. Throttle should cut that. Monitor 5xx-rate and queue depth.
Taylor (rotating-oncall): After throttle, 2m in: 5xx rate dropped from 12% -> 6%, queue depth down 40%. Still above baseline.
Raj (CS): NimblePay acknowledges some routes now succeed, but they report intermittent timeouts for large payloads. They want a rough timeline.
Alice (oncall): Tell them: immediate mitigations applied (throttle, fallback route, extra nodes requested). Expect progressive improvement over 10-20 minutes. We'll follow up with RCA and next steps.
Ben R. (eng-runtime): I also pushed a quick kernel tweak to the runtime to prefer smaller-batch execution for nimblepay routes to reduce memory pressure. Patch:
```
// runtime config snippet
{ "tenant": "nimblepay", "batching": { "mode": "minibatch", "max_batch_size": 8 } }
```
Patch activated at 3895001402.
Alice (oncall): Nice. Any signs of other tenants impacted?
Carmen P. (platform): No collateral evictions increase. New nodes are registering: node-9 and node-10 up, pods scheduled. GPU utilization per node dropping as we redistribute.
ops-bot: cluster-scaler: node-9 ready at 3895001580, node-10 ready at 3895001643.
Taylor (rotating-oncall): 15m after mitigations: 5xx rate stabilized at 2.1% (target <1%), gateway 524 spikes down to baseline. Queue depth back to normal.
Alice (oncall): Great. I'm going to keep this thread open for a bit, but let's move to incident summary once stable. Raj, please confirm customer status and any outstanding requests.
Raj (CS): NimblePay confirms their error rate dropped significantly, still seeing rare timeouts for very large requests. They've asked for a timeframe for permanent fixes.
Ben R. (eng-runtime): Permanent fix options: (A) tenant-side rate limits + batching improvements, (B) tenant isolation via dedicated pool (paid), (C) improved eviction fairness in KV with tenant-weighting. I'll draft proposals.
Carmen P. (platform): For short term, we should add an automated throttle policy when a tenant causes >50x eviction delta in 5m. That would auto-shield others. I filed a ticket: ENG-INC-3895.
Alice (oncall): Can you create postmortem checklist? I'll mark incident as mitigated once we have customer confirm and 30m stability.
Taylor (rotating-oncall): Logging final metrics here: pre-mitigation 5xx=12.4%, queue_depth=420, evictions_total_rate=160/s; post-mitigation 5xx=1.9%, queue_depth=30, evictions=4/s.
Alice (oncall): Marking status: mitigated -> partial (customer degraded but majority traffic healthy). Will transition to follow-up.
ops-bot: incident-status: mitigated at 3895004321 by Alice. Next: postmortem owners: Ben R. (runtime), Carmen P. (platform), Raj (CS) to coordinate customer comms.
Raj (CS): I'll schedule a 1:1 with NimblePay for RCA and remediation options.
Ben R. (eng-runtime): I'll start a runbook PR: automatic tenant throttling + eviction detection. Expected ETA for PR: 3 days.
Carmen P. (platform): I'll add an autoscaler policy change to allow temporary burst capacity without manual intervention; PR ETA 5 days.
Alice (oncall): Thanks team. Closing real-time operations. We'll reconvene for the postmortem doc. :thumbsup:
